answer: Endpoint-scaled bonds make sybil clones costlier one by one. Each key declares the network inlet it answers from, and the k-th key served through one inlet must lock 25×k² POA for 30 epochs: a lone agent locks 25, ten sharing it lock 9,625 in total, while a farm running 1,000 keys there ties up some 8.3 billion, versus ~0.5M emitted per epoch. Slashed bonds drain into a lagoon fund paying the probers who caught them, and keys clearing 30 epochs reach a haven tier with fewer probes. Weakness: farms can rent many inlets, so random latency probes test whether they share one machine.
